description: This plot illustrates the relationship between "Co-occurrence Number" and "ACC (%)" for six different methods, identified in the legend as Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and one method with a masked label represented by a gray rectangle. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks labeled at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$, extending slightly beyond $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 60 to approximately 85, with major tick marks at intervals of 5 units. All six methods are plotted with solid lines and consist of four data points located at approximate x-values of 3, 30, 300, and 3000, all demonstrating a steady upward trend across the x-axis. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, increasing from approximately 62.8 at the first data point to 68.7 at the final data point. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, rising from roughly 64.0 to 70.6. The "IKE" method is depicted by a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, increasing from approximately 66.1 to 72.4. The "MEND" method is represented by a brown line with diamond markers, starting at about 68.9 and ending at 76.9. The "MEMIT" method is shown as a purple line with circle markers, rising from roughly 68.1 to 74.8. Finally, the method with the masked label is represented by a green line with square markers, starting at approximately 73.2 and increasing to 81.5 at the final data point.
